title: Fix streaming metering edge cases: ensure accurate per-stream token accounting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:

We observed multiple customer reports and internal alerts where streaming calls (server-sent chunks / chunked HTTP and websockets) result in incorrect billed token counts. Errors fall into 3 buckets: (1) reconnects and resumed streams cause duplicated output accounting, (2) partial chunk flushes (e.g., early truncation + later finalization) lead to mismatched input/output attribution, (3) aborted streams produce invoiceable tokens with no corresponding completion record.

Goals:
- Ensure per-stream token accounting is deterministic and idempotent across reconnections and retries.
- Maintain compatibility with existing non-streaming metering pipeline.
- Add end-to-end tests and monitoring to prevent regressions.

Background & root cause hypothesis:
- The metering pipeline currently increments token counts on two different events: chunk_emitted (client-facing streaming chunk) and response_finalized (completion). When a client reconnects, the runtime replays pending chunks; both the replay and the original recorded chunks were persisted, yielding duplicate counts.
- Streaming proxies sometimes split logical tokens across frames; our token counter treats frames as independent events, so partial frames can be double-counted when reassembly occurs later.
- Aborted streams (network failure) emit chunk events but never reach the reconciliation job that marks them as non-billable or reconciled.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Introduce a server-assigned stream_session_id for every streaming session. This id is authoritative for metering and survives client reconnects when a resume is requested.
2) Attach per-chunk sequence_id and running_token_offset (both integers) to every chunk event emitted by the runtime. Metering service will only accept chunk events with monotonically increasing sequence_id per stream_session_id. Duplicates or replays with the same sequence_id are ignored.
3) Update event schema (old events remain readable): add stream_session_id:string, sequence_id:int, final_chunk:boolean, token_count:int, running_token_offset:int. Implement backward-compat handling for non-stream events (null session id).
4) Reconciliation rules: if a stream_session_id is abandoned (no final_chunk within X minutes), create a "timed-out" reconciliation record that credits back incomplete or uncertain tokens based on policy (e.g., only bill committed final tokens).
5) Add a short-lived in-memory cache (LRU per runtime node) of recent (stream_session_id, last_sequence_id) to quickly drop duplicate replays at the source and avoid persistent DB writes.
6) Billing ledger: make adjustments idempotent by recording operation_id for every increment so replays can be ignored. Operation_id = stream_session_id + sequence_id.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Option A (chosen): server-generated stream_session_id + sequence_id gives strong correctness and is straightforward to enforce at metering layer, but requires a small runtime schema change and minor protocol bump for streaming clients.
- Option B (rely on client idempotency tokens): avoids touching runtime but depends on diverse client implementations and is brittle for third-party SDKs.
- Option C (post-hoc heuristics in reconciliation): low runtime change but yields possible over/under-billing windows and complex refund processes.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Triage by Aisha: Elevated to P0 after 3 customer escalations and spikes in billing error rates. Assigned to Marco for investigation.

2026-03-02 — Marco: Reproduced duplication locally using a curl-based streaming replay test. Repro steps attached to attachments. Observed duplicate DB writes for chunk events when the client reconnects with resume=true.

2026-03-03 — Design sync with runtime: agreed to add server_assigned stream_session_id. Runtime owners flagged a minor protocol bump for websocket resume semantics (ETA for runtime change: 2 sprints).

2026-03-04 — Decision note: Use sequence_id + running_token_offset. Sequence_id guarantees monotonicity; running_token_offset allows safe reconciliation of split-frame tokens. We will ignore older events if sequence_id <= last_seen.

2026-03-05 — Engineering: Implemented event schema changes in metering service (branch: feat/stream-session-metering). Added DB migration to add OperationRecords with operation_id. Running unit tests locally.

2026-03-07 — QA: Added e2e test harness that simulates network flaps and resume semantics. Found one edge case where unordered delivery from proxy hit the metering service out-of-order — fixed by buffering until sequence_id gap is filled or timeout.

2026-03-09 — PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/11842 — metering: add stream_session_id and sequence_id enforcement. Includes unit tests and integration test harness. Requesting runtime review.

2026-03-10 — Observability: Dashboard alert created (billing.stream-dup-rate) and temporary retroactive job started to scan last 7 days for duplicates and emit adjustment transactions. Retro job link: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/streams/stream-metrics
